The New Jersey-based firm recorded $141.1M in revenue for the quarter with 5% YoY growth and a 13% rise, sequentially beating the consensus by roughly $3M as Asceniv added $124.7M to the top line.

Raymond James analyst Ryan Deschner attributed the quarterly beat to Asceniv, sales of which climbed ~31% YoY and ~21% QoQ due to rising physician adoption, new patient starts, and expanding end-user utilization.
“Favorable demand trends have continued into the fourth quarter, highlighting the durability of ASCENIV’s growth trajectory and significant remaining market opportunity," said ADMA

However, the company reaffirmed its 2026 outlook for topline, indicating at least $530M in revenue amid favorable but stable utilization trends for Bivigam, its plasma-derived IVIG product indicated for primary immunodeficiency.
